posts.idea: Weekly set report: a report card with fixed fields (new count, on the walls, year total, walls open or stripped), a first-timer problem and a setter's pick
Problem label: a museum-style label for one named problem, credited to its setter
Dictionary-entry card for gym vocabulary, starting with 'beta (n.)'
Two ways in: one existing session shown as two unlabelled entry options, after the run-club schedule
Same tag, different problems: two problems with the same grade tag and each setter's line on why it feels different
You will fall: a first-timer carousel about the floor and how to fall
Spread inside one grade: depends on whether the gym logs ascents

promised_sections.section: 1. Make this first: the set report
promised_sections.note: Fully specified: format, cover fields, slides, hook, caption job and failure mode.

promised_sections.section: 2. It works in another niche. your version.
promised_sections.note: Four adaptations from other niches, each with slides and a hook. It also names one idea it rejected and says why.
Two new ideas plus a ranking of the earlier ones.
Dated trend notes with sources. Says openly that there is no community or Reddit data.

promised_sections.section: 5. Well made, and what we could establish about it
promised_sections.note: Only one reference (upa!). It is thin but gives a usable takeaway.
Gaps, inferences and a source list. Mostly process notes and of little use to the creator.

price_why: It gives a freelancer who designs for a gym a repeatable weekly carousel format and five more ready-to-design carousel concepts they can bring to the setters this week. The research apparatus pads it, so it isn't worth more.
one_line: A heavily sourced brief that leads with a fixed-field weekly 'set report' carousel and ranks five more carousel concepts for members and first-timers.
strongest: The set report is a distinctive, repeatable format built from counts the setters already have, with fields, slides, hook, caption job and failure mode all specified.
weakest: Research jargon and process notes (taste lines, `the reader cannot produce the ground`, tool-block logs, config remarks) bury the useful concepts. Several hooks are also blanks the gym has to fill in.
